title: Isolation and in vitro cultivation of adrenal cells from mice
protocol: Prepare four small petri dishes filled with PBS and place them on ice.
Prepare tools for dissection: forceps and scissors.
Preheat digestion buffer to 37°C.
Preheat culture medium to 37°C.
Collect adrenals from mice.
Sacrifice the mouse according to regional animal welfare regulations or approved experimental protocols.
Spray 80% ethanol on the fur of the mouse (abdomen) to avoid contamination.
Cut the abdominal wall in the middle (linea alba) from bottom to top until the beginning of the diaphragm.
Make a window by cutting at the top and bottom ends of the previous cut, both right and left.
Open the peritoneum as previously described for the abdominal wall.
Carefully move the organs (intestine, liver) to the left side using forceps.
Lift up the left part of the liver to make the right kidney and adrenal gland visible.
Dissect the right adrenal gland by grabbing fat around the gland with a curved forceps without squeezing it.
Place the dissected adrenal gland in a petri dish containing PBS on ice.
Carefully move the organs to the right side using forceps.
Lift up the stomach and spleen to make the left kidney and adrenal gland visible.
Dissect the left adrenal gland by grabbing fat around the gland with a curved forceps without squeezing it.
Place the adrenal in a petri dish with PBS.
Repeat the dissection for the remaining mice and pool all adrenals in one petri dish.
Transfer all adrenals to a new petri dish with ice-cold PBS using curved forceps.
Remove fat surrounding the adrenal gland carefully with two forceps.
Peel off and discard excess fat on a paper towel next to the petri dish.
Put the cleaned adrenal glands into a new petri dish filled with PBS on ice.
Continue holding the adrenal gland gently without compressing it.
Place the petri dish containing all cleaned adrenal glands under the stereomicroscope.
Open one side of an adrenal gland carefully and peel off the cortex gradually.
Observe as the medulla becomes visible and the PBS gets cloudy due to the removed cortex pieces.
Transfer remaining adrenal glands to a new petri dish with fresh PBS if the current solution is too murky.
Use curved forceps to transfer the medulla into a new petri dish filled with PBS carefully.
Continue processing the remaining adrenal glands in the same manner.
Transfer the contents of the petri dishes containing either cortex or medulla to separate 50 mL tubes using a 1000 μL pipette.
Try to remove all tissue by pipetting up and down gently.
Centrifuge for 5 minutes at 270 × g at room temperature (20°C–25°C).
Remove and discard the PBS supernatant using a 1000 μL pipette.
Add 5 mL digestion buffer to the 50 mL tubes containing the cortex and medulla, respectively.
Place the tubes in a shaking water bath at 37°C for 20 minutes.
Resuspend the remaining tissue parts by pipetting up and down approximately 50 times using a 1000 μL pipette.
Centrifuge for 5 minutes at 270 × g at room temperature.
Remove and discard the supernatant from both 50 mL tubes.
Add 5 mL PBS to each 50 mL tube.
Centrifuge for 5 minutes at 270 × g at room temperature.
Remove and discard the supernatant from the medullary cells tube.
Resuspend the cell pellet in 500 μL culture medium with bFGF.
Add the suspension to an Easy strainer with a 100 μm pore size.
Add another 500 μL of the same medium to ensure all cells pass through the strainer.
Remove and discard the supernatant from the cortical cells tube.
Resuspend the cell pellet in 500 μL culture medium with bFGF.
Add the suspension to an Easy strainer with a 100 μm pore size.
Add another 500 μL to the strainer to ensure all cells pass through.
Seed each cell suspension in one well of an ultra-low attachment surface 24-well plate.
Culture the cells for 16–24 hours in the incubator at 37°C and 5% CO2.
Transfer cells to a 15 mL tube using a 1000 μL pipette.
Centrifuge the cells at 270 × g for 5 minutes.
Remove old medium from the cells.
Resuspend the cells in fresh cell culture medium containing bFGF.
Transfer cells to a new well of the 24-well plate.
Change medium every 3–4 days by carefully removing half of the medium.
Add an equal amount of new culture medium (totaling 1 mL/well) containing bFGF.
Coat a 24-well plate or an 8-well chamber slide with poly-D-lysine for 16–24 hours (300 μL/well, 1 mg/mL poly-D-lysine in PBS) at 37°C.
Wash wells three times carefully with PBS.
Add Fibronectin (300 μL/well, 0.6 nM in PBS) and incubate for 3 hours at 37°C in the incubator.
Wash wells three times carefully with PBS.
Transfer spheroids to an 1.5 mL tube using a 1000 μL pipette.
Centrifuge for 5 minutes at 270 × g.
Add 1 mL new culture medium without bFGF.
Distribute spheroids to all chambers and fill up with medium (300 μL/well).
Medium should be changed twice per week by removing old medium and adding new.
